name: svg-path-commander
category: A4. Vector, typography, diagrams and stills
role: SVG path-string maths in Node: normalise to cubics, transform, measure, no DOM
summary: TypeScript library (svg-path-commander) that parses an SVG path string and normalises it to absolute cubic segments, converts arcs, reverses, optimises, applies matrix transforms and reports length, bounding box and point-at-length, all in Node with no DOM. Its strength is the path-data step a morph needs before any renderer: two different paths reduced to comparable cubic control points, ahead of resvg.
use_when: Preparing two paths for a seekable shape morph; over svgo, which optimises whole files
Path length, bounding box or transforms on a path string without building a scene model; over paper-js or svg-js
Converting arcs, quadratics and shorthand curves to absolute cubics before frame generation
avoid_when: Whole-file SVG optimisation or ID cleanup: svgo
A scene graph with hit-testing, boolean ops or rendering: paper-js
Real 3D: its 3D transform is a perspective projection of the path
notes: 2026-11-27: it normalises but does not pair or split segments; two paths with 6 and 7 cubics after toCurve() stay unequal, so equal counts are the caller's job.
2026-11-27: toCurve() mutates the instance, so getTotalLength() afterwards measures the cubic approximation and differs slightly from a fresh instance.

assessment.rationale: npm svg-path-commander 2.4.0 published 2026-11-24, MIT. Only catalogue route for path-string normalisation without a DOM or scene model; svgo works on files, paper-js and svg-js hold a scene.

evidence.result: Two paths (H/A/L/Q and L/S/Q/H) both normalised to 6 absolute cubics, interpolated to 3 SVG frames identical across two Node 22.19.0 processes; translate moved bbox x by 5; resvg 0.47.0 PNGs 260x260 inspected.
evidence.scope: toCurve, transform, getBBox and getTotalLength on two single-subpath paths, macOS arm64; not getPointAtLength, optimize, reverse, 3D, unequal segment counts or browser use.
